This binding is supported by the presence of an enzyme inhibitor relationship between Sulindac and Ptgs1, indicating a direct inhibitory effect on the enzyme. The final score of 0.5854 suggests a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, which is consistent with the known pharmacological properties of Sulindac as a selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitor. The integration of this evidence with the broader context of Sulindac's classification as an enzyme inhibitor reinforces its role in modulating inflammatory responses by targeting Ptgs1. The mechanism is further supported by the presence of a lowest common ancestor (LCA) between Sulindac and Piroxicam, both of which are classified as organic molecules and enzyme inhibitors, highlighting a shared pharmacological profile.
